We release open-source code to support reproducible lifelong learning research.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31224/5919\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 3]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7286873\", \"title\": [\"Dual Memory System: A Method for Affective-Weighted Episodic–Semantic Memory Consolidation for Continual Learning in Autonomous Agents\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous agents operating over long horizons must retain specific experiences, generalize recurring structure, and decide which memories are worth keeping, without collapsing into an undifferentiated buffer that grows without bound or loses interpretability. We present a method for building such a system, the Dual Memory System (DMS), modeled on the brain&apos;s separation between a fast hippocampal episodic store and a slow neocortical semantic store, with an affective-weighting mechanism inspired by amygdala-gated consolidation. The method specifies how to encode experiences into dense embeddings and affect labels, rank them for rehearsal using an interpretable, decomposable importance function, cluster and abstract high-rehearsal memories into semantic records under an explicit faithfulness check, and decay low-importance records over time.
